paragraphs: Here's what I see in this passage, friend. Solomon doesn't start with a shovel. He starts with a purpose. He says the LORD told his father David, "I will put your son on your throne in your place, and he will build the house for My Name." (1 Kings 5:5). So the first thing under this temple isn't stone or cedar. It's a promise God made.

Now look at how the work gets done. Solomon asks for help from Hiram, king of Tyre, because there are none among them "as skilled in logging as the Sidonians." (1 Kings 5:6). Nobody gets a giant trophy for doing it all alone. Then Hiram says, "Blessed be the LORD this day!" (1 Kings 5:7), and a treaty and peace follow (1 Kings 5:12). I think that tells us good work for the LORD often takes more hands than ours, and it's a lot more fun with a crew. I know what a solo bakery feels like, and the crew wins.

And friend, the temple gets prepared before anybody lays one stone of it. Timber, stone, workers, order, all of it comes together first (1 Kings 5:17-18). That's why your quiet prep matters, even when it feels like nothing's happening yet. It's like me getting the dough ready while the oven's still warming up. The LORD gives wisdom and keeps His promises (1 Kings 5:12), so get ready with Him, and keep your ovens warm.
